atlas_neighbors_of_114.formal_statement: Is there A subset of N with density 0 and c>0 such that every graph on large enough vertices with avg degree >= c contains a cycle whose length is in A?
atlas_neighbors_of_114.resolution_technique: Bollobás-type density / cycle-length set arguments (graph theory)
atlas_neighbors_of_114.structural_similarity_to_114: Edge weight 0.79 is the strongest single edge in the 114-neighborhood but the morphism is structural-shape-only (both are 'forced structure from density/size'). Object class is graphs, not polynomials. Cross-domain edge.

atlas_neighbors_of_114.resolution_technique: Bernstein-Walsh / conformal-map / extremal-length / lemniscate-geometry (Borwein-Erdélyi line); NOT plain Markov/Bernstein per Perplexity call 3.
atlas_neighbors_of_114.structural_similarity_to_114: Same setting (monic p of deg n on lemniscate); but the functional bounded is sup of |p'| (analytic extremum), not arc length (geometric-measure invariant). Per Perplexity call 3: the proof toolkit (conformal mapping, extremal length) is philosophically related but does NOT cleanly transfer to a length-of-level-set bound.

atlas_neighbors_of_114.formal_statement: p(z)=prod(z-z_i) with |z_i|<=1: is planar Lebesgue measure |{z:|p(z)|<1}| > n - O(1)?
atlas_neighbors_of_114.resolution_technique: Subharmonic / potential-theoretic estimates for u=log|p|; Cartan-type exceptional-set covering; classical Pólya / Wagner / Pommerenke + recent AI-assisted (GPT-5.2 Pro) write-up per Perplexity call 1.
atlas_neighbors_of_114.structural_similarity_to_114: Same u=log|p|, same sublevel set construction. Per Perplexity call 1: technique controls 2D AREA of sublevel set, not 1D LENGTH of level set. A coarea-bridge (integral of |nabla u| dt = length of level set) is the conceptual route, but requires independent gradient control near {u=0} that the #116 toolkit does not supply.

atlas_neighbors_of_114.formal_statement: r_k(N) = size of largest subset of {1..N} with no non-trivial k-term AP; prove r_k(N) = o(N) (Szemerédi).
atlas_neighbors_of_114.resolution_technique: Szemerédi's theorem / hypergraph regularity / Gowers norms.
atlas_neighbors_of_114.structural_similarity_to_114: Edge labeled technique-transfer but technique is additive-combinatorial / structure-vs-randomness. Off-topic for polynomial-lemniscate analytic geometry. Atlas tag appears to be a generic 'extremal threshold' similarity, not a transferable proof tactic.

atlas_neighbors_of_114.formal_statement: Exists Littlewood flat polynomial: P of degree n with +-1 coeffs, sqrt(n) << |P(z)| << sqrt(n) for all |z|=1?
atlas_neighbors_of_114.resolution_technique: Balister-Bollobás-Morris-Sahasrabudhe (BBMS, 2019/2020); probabilistic + combinatorial construction of near-flat sign polynomials on unit circle.
atlas_neighbors_of_114.structural_similarity_to_114: Per Perplexity call 4: NO direct route. #228 controls L^infty value of P on the fixed circle |z|=1 under +-1 coefficient constraint. #114 asks for arc length of level set {|p|=1} for ARBITRARY monic p. Different observable, different object class. BBMS machinery does not transfer.

atlas_neighbors_of_114.formal_statement: Exists polynomial f:Z->Z of deg>=2 and A subset Z s.t. every n in Z is uniquely n=a+b with a in A, b in {f(k):k in Z}?
atlas_neighbors_of_114.resolution_technique: Open. Additive basis / perfect-difference family techniques.
atlas_neighbors_of_114.structural_similarity_to_114: Generalization tag is purely structural (both involve a polynomial). Object class is additive number theory, not complex-analytic arc length. No technique transfer route identified.

atlas_neighbors_of_114.formal_statement: Monic f of deg n: for every c>1, does {z:|f(z)|<1} have at most O_c(1) connected components of diameter > c (constant indep of n)?
atlas_neighbors_of_114.resolution_technique: Disproven by counterexample (Pommerenke-type root-clustering construction per Perplexity call 2 family).
atlas_neighbors_of_114.structural_similarity_to_114: Same sublevel set, same monic-poly class. Counterexample controls TOPOLOGY (number-of-components / diameter) not LENGTH. Per Perplexity call 2: disproof constructions do not refute or support #114 directly; root-clustering is the shared phenomenon but does not break the conjectured |L| <= 2n+O(1) extremum.

atlas_neighbors_of_114.formal_statement: All except o(2^n) +-1-coefficient degree-n polynomials f have |f(z)|<1 for some |z|=1?
atlas_neighbors_of_114.resolution_technique: BBMS-adjacent: probabilistic + counting (second moment) on Littlewood polynomial values on unit circle per Perplexity call 4.
atlas_neighbors_of_114.structural_similarity_to_114: Same family as #228 (Littlewood). Per Perplexity call 4: no transfer to arc-length problem on unconstrained monic polynomials.

atlas_neighbors_of_114.formal_statement: Lagrange interpolation: given nodes a^n_i in [-1,1], unique deg n-1 interpolants p^n_i; behavior of L_n f(x) = sum f(a^n_i) p^n_i(x)?
atlas_neighbors_of_114.structural_similarity_to_114: Polynomial-deg-n machinery but functional (Lebesgue constant of interpolation operator) is unrelated to complex-plane lemniscate arc length. No transfer route.

atlas_neighbors_of_114.formal_statement: Size Ramsey number R-hat(P_n) for path P_n: is R-hat(P_n) = O(n)?
atlas_neighbors_of_114.structural_similarity_to_114: Edge labeled technique-transfer but the techniques are graph-Ramsey. Off-topic for arc length of polynomial lemniscates. Atlas tag spurious.

atlas_neighbors_of_114.formal_statement: Monic f, E={|f|<1} connected: is E contained in a disc of radius 2?
atlas_neighbors_of_114.resolution_technique: Disproven by Pommerenke-line root-clustering constructions (counterexample polynomials with roots near unit circle producing 'arms' of E extending past radius 2). Per Perplexity call 2.
atlas_neighbors_of_114.structural_similarity_to_114: Same E={|f|<1} object. Per Perplexity call 2: counterexamples to #1046 are NOT the extremizers for #114; they control containment-of-E, not length-of-boundary. No technique transfer.

atlas_neighbors_of_114.formal_statement: Monic f with m distinct roots, c small s.t. {|f|<=c} has m components: is E={|f|<1} in disc of radius <=2?
atlas_neighbors_of_114.structural_similarity_to_114: Same E and monic-poly class. Same conclusion as #1046: topology counterexample, not length counterexample. No transfer.

atlas_neighbors_of_114.formal_statement: Monic f, all roots |z|<=r<2: must E={|f|<1} have a component containing 0?
atlas_neighbors_of_114.resolution_technique: Disproven (root-clustering construction makes origin land in a different component).
atlas_neighbors_of_114.structural_similarity_to_114: Same E, monic class, root-radius parameter. Per Perplexity call 2: counterexample is about component-containment, orthogonal to arc-length. No transfer.

atlas_neighbors_of_114.formal_statement: Real polynomial deg n with real roots a_0 < ... < a_n in AP: behavior of root differences?
atlas_neighbors_of_114.structural_similarity_to_114: Same constraint-parallel tag but the object class (real-rooted polynomials with AP roots) is geometrically far from monic-complex-coefficient lemniscate length. No transfer.

atlas_neighbors_of_114.formal_statement: Monic f, all roots |z|<=1, E={|f|<=1}: shortest curve in E containing all roots — what is its minimum length?
atlas_neighbors_of_114.resolution_technique: Open. Clunie-Netanyahu path existence (path from 0 to |z|=1 in E) is the closest classical positive result. Steiner-tree-in-algebraic-set intuition per Perplexity call 3.
atlas_neighbors_of_114.structural_similarity_to_114: STRONGEST OPEN ANALOG. Same monic-poly class, same E, same parameter n; dual problem (shortest INSIDE curve vs longest BOUNDARY curve). Per Perplexity call 3: there is NO known theorem that the shortest curve in E containing roots lies on the boundary {|f|=1}, so a #1120 lower bound does not directly imply a #114 upper bound. Thematic dual but not provable bridge.

atlas_neighbors_of_114.formal_statement: Exists c>0: for all large n, all +-1-coefficient deg-n P have max_{|z|=1} |P(z)| >= sqrt(n) + c·(something)?
atlas_neighbors_of_114.resolution_technique: Open. Erdős sup-norm lower-bound for Littlewood polynomials; tied to BBMS/Konyagin/Kahane probabilistic toolkit.
atlas_neighbors_of_114.structural_similarity_to_114: Littlewood family (+-1 coeffs, sup on fixed |z|=1). Per Perplexity call 4: no transfer to arc-length-on-arbitrary-monic problem.

top_3_transfer_candidates.technique: Subharmonic potential theory for u = log|p(z)|; Cartan-type exceptional-set covering by disks; area estimate of sublevel set |{u<0}|.
top_3_transfer_candidates.structural_link_to_114: Same u = log|p|, same sublevel set {u<0} vs same level set {u=0}. Both depend on root geometry of monic p of degree n.
top_3_transfer_candidates.hypothesis: If one can extend the #116 potential-theoretic toolkit by adding a coarea-formula step (integral of |nabla u| over the plane = integral over t of H^1({u=t})), with usable pointwise lower bounds on |nabla u| = |p'/p| near the level {u=0}, one could in principle convert a sublevel-set area estimate into a level-set length estimate. This is the conceptual bridge identified by Perplexity call 1 but it requires an independent gradient-control input that the #116 proof does not provide. The Fryntov-Nazarov 2008 paper (arXiv:0808.0717) already uses Stokes / log-derivative pole decomposition / Cauchy on |p'|^2 area integral, which is the genuine analytic primitive here. Transfer is real but NOT a shortcut: it lands the attack back in the existing Fryntov-Nazarov / Tao 2512.12455 toolbox, which is already in active use in the 114 proof_path program.

top_3_transfer_candidates.technique: Steiner-tree-in-algebraic-set + Clunie-Netanyahu path existence in E = {|f|<=1}.
top_3_transfer_candidates.structural_link_to_114: Same monic poly class, same n, dual extremization: #1120 is infimum-length INSIDE E, #114 is supremum-length OF BOUNDARY of E. Both controlled by the same root geometry.
top_3_transfer_candidates.hypothesis: A linear lower bound length(gamma) >= cn on the shortest interior curve connecting roots inside E might force the boundary {|f|=1} to have at least an O(n)-comparable length, by an isoperimetric or Steiner-tree-vs-boundary comparison argument. Per Perplexity call 3, there is NO known structural theorem identifying the shortest interior connector with a boundary component, so the bridge is speculative. Worth keeping on the radar as a dual problem but not actionable.

top_3_transfer_candidates.technique: Bernstein-Walsh extremal-polynomial inequality + conformal-map / extremal-length / lemniscate-geometry machinery (Borwein-Erdélyi line).
top_3_transfer_candidates.structural_link_to_114: Connectedness hypothesis on {|p|<=1} matches the lemniscate setting of #114. Both control derivative behavior of p on its critical level.
top_3_transfer_candidates.hypothesis: If one had a sharp pointwise upper bound on |p'(z)| at the level {|p|=1} (rather than the #115 sup-of-derivative-over-disk bound), one could integrate around {|p|=1} to bound the arc length. But |L| = integral_{|p|=1} 1 ds, and ds is not directly an integral of |p'|; the right substitute is the Stokes reduction |L| = 2 Re int_E partial-s dA used in Fryntov-Nazarov. Per Perplexity call 3, the Bernstein-Walsh technology is philosophically related but no clean transfer exists. Same destination (Fryntov-Nazarov toolkit) as candidate #1.

intractability_reasoning: Of 16 curated-graph neighbors of #114 in the Atlas (scout + dense, excluding 123 low-signal cross_corpus edges): (a) 4 disproven topology-of-sublevel-set problems (#511, #1046, #1047, #1048) have counterexamples that control component topology and containment in discs, NOT level-set arc length, and per Perplexity call 2 do not refute #114. (b) 4 solved Littlewood +-1-coefficient problems and #228/#525 in this family use BBMS probabilistic + counting machinery on a fixed circle |z|=1, which per Perplexity call 4 does not transfer to arc-length-of-level-set on unconstrained monic polynomials. (c) The strongest open structural analog #1120 is a DUAL problem (shortest interior connector vs longest boundary) with no known structural theorem linking the two extremization directions per Perplexity call 3. (d) Solved polynomial problems #115, #116, #1114 are governed by Bernstein-Walsh / potential-theoretic / real-rooted machinery; per Perplexity calls 1 and 3 the techniques are philosophically related but require an additional coarea-or-Stokes step to convert area/derivative bounds to length bounds, and that step is exactly the Fryntov-Nazarov 2008 + Tao 2512.12455 toolkit ALREADY in the 114 proof_path program. (e) The off-domain solved problems #72 (graphs), #139 (Szemerédi), #720 (size-Ramsey) carry Atlas edge labels (structural, technique-transfer) that on inspection are generic 'forced-structure-from-density' similarities, not transferable proof tactics. Conclusion: the Atlas neighborhood offers NO non-brute-force shortcut to #114; the live attack continues to be the existing Fryntov-Nazarov + Tao asymptotic-improvement chain plus the finite-n<=14 bridge program documented in the 75 prior EXP-MATH-EHP114-* experiment dirs.

perplexity_calls_log.verdict: Subharmonic + Cartan area-estimate; NOT directly applicable to arc length; coarea-formula bridge is conceptual only.
Pommerenke-line root-clustering counterexamples; control topology, NOT length; do not refute #114.
No known theorem links shortest-interior to longest-boundary; #115 uses Bernstein-Walsh + conformal mapping, no clean transfer.
L^infty-on-fixed-circle technology does NOT transfer to arc-length-on-arbitrary-monic; orthogonal problem class.
